sample_unit: simulated clinical case (scored outputs from six LLMs)
models_evaluated: NYAAI (New Youth Anesthesia Artificial Intelligence Assistant)

links.outcome: Guideline compliance and completeness of perioperative recommendations, including omissions of protocols
links.effect: NYAAI omitted temperature management and delirium protocols; general-purpose models showed moderate guideline compliance (ChatGPT 4/5; Gemini 3/5) but produced contextually inappropriate recommendations.
links.quote: However, it exhibited selective guideline adherence, omitting temperature management and delirium protocols.

links.outcome: Addressing extreme-event or emergency protocols (aortic rupture management) in perioperative recommendations
links.effect: Safety redundancy was a universal failure: no model addressed extreme-event protocols such as aortic rupture management.
links.quote: Safety redundancy emerged as a universal failure—no model addressed extreme-event protocols (aortic rupture management).

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks six LLMs on a simulated clinical case evaluated by anesthesiologists across guidelines, applicability, and safety dimensions, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
